Situation
A patient with lung cancer, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension, recovering post-ICU from sepsis with an active chest tube in situ, requires review of a Lower Limb (LL) Doppler study and a recent Chest X-Ray (CXR).
Background
Primary Diagnosis: Lung cancer, creating a high-risk baseline for hypercoagulability, thromboembolic events, and progressive pulmonary compromise.
Comorbidities: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and Hypertension, requiring tight metabolic and hemodynamic oversight.
Hospital Course: Admitted to the ICU for severe sepsis, subsequently stabilized, and managed with chest tube insertion for pleural space intervention. 
Assessment
Pulmonary & Thoracic: Active chest tube requires ongoing assessment for output volume, character, air leaks, and insertion site integrity. Recent CXR is needed to evaluate tube placement, lung expansion, and resolution of pleural pathology.
Vascular & Perfusion: LL Doppler is indicated to rule out Deep Vein Thrombosis (DVT), a major risk factor given malignancy, immobility, and post-septic systemic inflammation.
Systemic Stability: Monitoring required for recovery from sepsis, maintenance of blood pressure parameters, and blood glucose control under physiological stress.
Recommendation
Diagnostic Review: Analyze the recent CXR to confirm proper chest tube positioning and check for adequate pulmonary re-expansion or residual effusion/pneumothorax. Interpret the LL Doppler findings to guide immediate initiation or adjustment of prophylactic versus therapeutic anticoagulation.
Clinical Monitoring: Track daily inflammatory markers, renal function panels, and complete blood counts to ensure complete clearance of the septic episode.
Nursing Interventions: Perform routine sterile dressing changes for the chest tube site, record strict fluid balance and output volumes, and implement mechanical or pharmacological DVT prophylaxis as cleared by the Doppler results.
